text:
olivia_support: FYI customer NovaForms is hitting 504s + 5xx from our hosted gateway for the past 20m. They say it started after a spike of long prompts. Escalating.

jordan_sre: Got it. Any request IDs or example payloads we can repro with?

olivia_support: Sent a sample earlier in the ticket, but here's the payload snippet they used: 
```json
{
  "model": "open-long-16k",
  "input": "<~6k token survey + embedded CSV>",
  "stream": false
}
```
They reported timeouts around 30s and gateway 502/504. Customer seeing failures ~p95 on their side.

maria_ops: Poking the logs for that tenant now. I see a lot of "enqueue: queue depth exceeded" and batcher backpressure warnings. Paste: 
```
2026-03-17T09:14:02Z ingress[gw-34]: enqueue failed tenant=novaforms err="queue depth limit (320) exceeded" route=hosted/generate
2026-03-17T09:14:05Z batcher[cb-7]: continuous-batcher backlog=128 active_batches=3 avg_seq=5200 kv_cache_spinup=true
2026-03-17T09:14:32Z runtime[inst-2]: request 5xx code=504 reason="timeout waiting for batch" worker=slot-45
```

sanjay_infra: That kv_cache_spinup=true is suspicious — long sequences cause big KV memory and stall batcher until warm. Continuous batching is queueing up short requests behind long ones. We're hitting per-route queue depth and starting to reject new inflight requests.

jordan_sre: Can we confirm if this is primarily long-sequence dominated or a general burst? Maria, do you have histograms for seq_len for that tenant in the window?

maria_ops: Histogram shows a heavy tail: 5% of requests >4k tokens but they consume ~60% of token-time due to decode. Batcher backlog timeline attached (snip): "backlog spikes align with longseq bursts at :10 and :30 minutes".

olivia_support: Customer also mentioned auth flaps earlier but they were unrelated — token rotation happened around :03 but no linked errors in logs. Billing shows normal usage.

sanjay_infra: Short-term mitigation options:
- 1) Rate-limit long-seq requests by route (quota/soft-limit)
- 2) Increase per-route queue depth and add a temp burst pool (risk: higher mem/cost)
- 3) Reroute NovaForms to dedicated pool with larger slot sizes (needs tenancy change)
- 4) Thundering-herd protection: prioritize small requests in batcher (preferential scheduling)

jordan_sre: For immediate relief I can: bump queue depth threshold on the gateway for that route from 320 -> 640 for a 1-hour window and enable prefer-small-requests scheduling. Will run canary on a single AZ first.

maria_ops: I have a quick CLI to apply gate changes:
```bash
# increase per-route queue depth
redwoodctl routes update --route hosted/generate --queue-depth 640 --scope tenant:novaforms --for 3600
# toggle small-request prioritization
redwoodctl batchers patch cb-7 --prefer-small true
```

I'll watch eviction logs. Note: changing queue depth needs SRE sign-off for memory risk. @jordan_sre pls ack.

jordan_sre: Ack, go ahead for canary in us-east-1 only. I'll monitor p95 and 5xx rates.

ingress-bot: [alert] route=hosted/generate tenant=novaforms p95_latency=18.2s p99_latency=54.7s queue_depth=320 -> 640 (canary us-east-1)

(30s pass)

maria_ops: Canary looks promising — p99 dropped from 54s -> 22s in us-east-1 and new rejects fell to near zero. No OOMs on cb-7 yet but mem headroom is thin (+12%).

sanjay_infra: Medium-term: we should add adaptive splitting for long requests (break into sub-batches or async processing) and make KV-cache pre-warm heuristics better so long runs don't stall small ones. I'll open infra-issue and propose a rollout.

jordan_sre: Also add a runbook step: when queue depth exceeded for a tenant, first check sequence-length histogram, then either (a) apply per-tenant queue bump canary or (b) apply tenant-level rate-limiter on long-seq endpoints. Documented mitigation below: 
```
Runbook excerpt: Quick mitigation for queue-saturation tail timeouts:
1) identify offending tenant and time window
2) capture seq_len histogram and KV spin events
3) apply per-route queue bump (canary) + prefer-small scheduling
4) if memory >75% escalate to infra lead and consider dedicated pool
5) communicate to customer: temporary throttling for long requests or suggest splitting
```

olivia_support: I'll message NovaForms with two options: temporary throttling guidance, or option to migrate to dedicated. Also asked them for a smaller repro set to validate.

maria_ops: After 45m of monitoring, I see the canary in us-east still healthy. Planning to roll to other AZs in 15m if no regressions. Leaving notes in the incident ticket.

jordan_sre: Thanks all. Follow-ups: sanjay please create infra ticket for adaptive-split/kv-warm; olivia please copy communication to customer and close loop once they confirm repro is mitigated.

olivia_support: Will do. :thumbsup:

(Note: thread created from incident alert at 6177777777)
